rule: Show users sample prompts and parameters to educate and inspire AI use.
quote: Share sample generations, prompts, and parameters to educate and inspire users.

rule: Solve the blank canvas problem by providing prompt suggestions or templates.
quote: Solves the blank canvas dilemma with clues for how to prompt.

rule: Use a distinct visual avatar to help users recognize and remember the AI.
quote: Visual identifier of the AI itself to help it be recognizable, memorable, and on-brand.

rule: Use display modes only when visual interaction improves the workflow.
quote: Use cards, carousels, fullscreen views, and other display modes only when visual interaction improves the workflow.

rule: Limit inline cards to two primary actions maximum.
quote: Limit to two actions, placed at bottom of card. Actions should perform either a conversation turn or a tool call.

rule: Prevent nested scrolling in cards; let them auto-fit content.
quote: Cards should auto fit their content and prevent internal scrolling.

rule: Keep carousels to 3–8 items for optimal readability and scannability.
quote: Keep to 3–8 items per carousel for readability.

rule: Reduce carousel metadata to three lines maximum for clarity.
quote: Reduce metadata to the most relevant details, with three lines max.

rule: Use consistent visual hierarchy across carousel cards.
quote: Use consistent visual hierarchy across cards.

rule: Validate AI interaction guidelines through user testing with design practitioners.
quote: validated through multiple rounds of evaluation including a user study with 49 design practitioners who tested the guidelines against 20 popular AI-infused products
finding: 49 design practitioners tested guidelines on 20 AI products

rule: Apply Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction early in your product design process.
quote: Use it early in your design process

rule: Prioritize which AI interaction guidelines to implement based on team planning.
quote: Your HAX Workbook session will result in prioritized work items for which Guidelines to implement first

rule: Mark all AI-generated content with a visible AI label for transparency.
quote: Use the AI label and styling to mark any instances of AI usage

rule: Use light-inspired visual effects to distinguish AI-generated content.
quote: Carbon for AI uses light-inspired effects like brightness, glow, and gradients to emphasize AI instances across the experience

rule: Use motion to bring clarity and character to AI experiences, showing users when content is being generated.
quote: Motion brings clarity and character to Rovo's AI experiences

rule: Establish a consistent tone of voice for AI that shows sound judgment and builds trust with users.
quote: Rovo's tone of voice shows sound judgment and builds trust for teams

rule: Show visual interaction only when it improves the workflow; avoid cards, carousels, and fullscreen views otherwise.
quote: Optional plugin UI can extend what users can do without breaking the flow of conversation. Use cards, carousels, fullscreen views, and other display modes only when visual interaction improves the workflow.

rule: Limit inline card actions to two maximum; place them at the bottom.
quote: Limit primary actions per card : Support up to two actions maximum, with one primary CTA and one optional secondary CTA.

rule: Do not nest multiple drill-ins, tabs, or deeper navigation within a card.
quote: No deep navigation or multiple views within a card. Cards should not contain multiple drill-ins, tabs, or deeper navigation.

rule: Cards must auto-fit content and prevent internal scrolling.
quote: No nested scrolling . Cards should auto fit their content and prevent internal scrolling.

rule: Keep carousels to 3–8 items for readability.
quote: Keep to 3–8 items per carousel for readability.

rule: Reduce carousel metadata to three lines maximum with the most relevant details.
quote: Reduce metadata to the most relevant details, with three lines max.

rule: Support semantic search so users find relevant results without knowing exact keywords.
quote: Elicit's semantic search means you don't have to know all the right keywords to get relevant results.

rule: Allow deep customization of AI outputs so users control which sources and information appear in reports.
quote: Unlike with other AI tools, Elicit Reports can be deeply customized. You can change which papers and what information is covered in the reports.

rule: Support all AI-generated claims with sentence-level citations from underlying sources for transparency.
quote: Elicit supports all AI-generated claims with sentence-level citations from the underlying sources.

rule: Measure and report time savings from automation so users understand the value gained.
quote: Researchers report up to 80% time savings using Elicit for systematic reviews.

rule: Let users add specific context with @ mentions to increase AI accuracy on focused questions.
quote: you can use @ to add context on specific files, symbols, remote repositories, or other non-code artifacts.

rule: Let users ignore selected repositories from AI results to control what context the system sees.
quote: Cody can ignore selected repositories from chat and autocomplete results, which helps you control and manage what context your codebase uses.

rule: Show file diffs for every edit so users review, modify, or revert agent changes before they persist.
quote: In VS Code and JetBrains, every edit shows up as a diff you can review, modify, or revert.

rule: Require explicit approval for every file edit and terminal command to keep users in control of what changes.
quote: Every file edit and terminal command requires your approval, so you stay in control of what actually changes.

rule: Track all agent changes with checkpoints so users can easily undo the agent's work.
quote: All changes are tracked with checkpoints, so you can easily undo the agent's work.

rule: Monitor and display linter and compiler errors in real time as the agent works, fixing issues before the user sees them.
quote: It monitors linter and compiler errors as it works, fixing issues like missing imports, type mismatches, and syntax errors before you even see them.

rule: Watch terminal output in real time and react to new output as it appears, catching compile errors and test failures.
quote: Cline continues working in the background and reacts to new output as it appears, catching compile errors, test failures, and server crashes as they happen.

rule: Use conversational UI to make collaborating with AI agents feel more approachable and natural.
quote: Slack's conversational UI makes collaborating more approachable, whether you're working with a colleague or an agent.

rule: Surface customer insights and CRM data alongside conversations so work progresses without context switching.
quote: Customer insights now live alongside conversations, so deals keep moving forward.

rule: Keep AI agents and teammates in the same workspace with shared context to align on ideas and refine together.
quote: Teammates and AI agents work in the same space with shared context. Generate new ideas, refine, and align—together.

rule: Separate conversation from task progress; show step-by-step execution in a collapsible, auditable panel.
quote: Chat worked while the agent did one task at a time and the conversation fit on a screen. As soon as agents started doing background work for minutes, firing tools in parallel, and keeping state over files, chat came up short.

rule: Transparency documents the system; explainability justifies one output. Build both, not one.
quote: Transparency and explainability solve different problems, and teams that treat them as one word ship half of what they need.

rule: Only 17% of teams mitigate explainability risk despite 40% naming it as key risk in AI adoption.
quote: 40% of respondents identified explainability as a key risk in adopting generative AI, yet only 17% said they were currently working to mitigate it
finding: 17% of teams mitigate explainability vs 40% who identify it as key risk

rule: Match explanation type to audience: engineers need debugging logs, users need domain language, auditors need system documentation.
quote: The right explanation depends on who is asking. A debugging engineer, a rejected applicant, and an auditor need three different artifacts from the same prediction.

rule: Integrate explanation design early in the system, not as a secondary afterthought.
quote: presenting explanations to the user is not trivial and is often left as a secondary aspect of the system's design process, leading to AI systems that are not useful to end-users
